hypothesis: On H200 the cuBLAS path leaves the router and some small-M projections well above the bandwidth floor. DeepGEMM BF16 NT, cuBLASLt, or a split-K streaming kernel is faster on those shapes. prepare() keeps a backend only when it beats torch on this GPU and stays inside tolerance, so a scored shape cannot regress.

roi_prior.component: router and M<=32 projections; large-M stays on whichever backend wins the local timing

fast_path: per scored (layer, m), the fastest of deep_gemm.bf16_gemm_nt, cublaslt_gemm_nt, and split-K
fallback: F.linear for BF16; FP32 matmul for router M<=8; BF16 hi+lo torch.mm above that
reject_if: geomean load time stays above 3200 us
a custom backend is selected and then loses to torch under CUDA-graph replay
